stories.headline: Serial Baltic drone airspace violations trigger Vilnius shelter alarm, force leaders underground, and expose civil-defence gaps
stories.summary: A suspected drone near the Belarus border caused Lithuania to issue a national air-raid alert on May 20, closing Vilnius airport for about an hour, driving President Nausėda and PM Ruginienė to underground bunkers, and prompting NATO jets to scramble. The incident was the most dramatic in a run of Baltic airspace violations stretching from May 17–23; Ruginienė later apologised for shelter-access failures, acknowledged systemic gaps before the Seimas, and ordered municipalities to keep shelters open 24 hours, while political commentary questioned her crisis-management competence.

stories.headline: Mass data theft from Lithuanian state property registry triggers PM's demand for director's resignation
stories.summary: Unknown third parties illegally accessed Lithuania's Real Estate and Legal Entities registers and copied over 600,000 records; the Prosecutor General's Office opened a pre-trial investigation and estimated damages at no less than €111,000. PM Ruginienė publicly called for the resignation of Registrų centras director Adrijus Jusas, who subsequently stepped down; opposition conservative Kasčiūnas extended criticism to Economy Minister Grikšas, and a separate political row erupted when parliamentarian Širinskienė claimed Ruginienė deleted her critical comment on the PM's Facebook post about the incident.

stories.headline: Balloon cigarette-smuggling bust ensnares 13 police and border officers, PM calls it unprecedented
stories.summary: Lithuanian law enforcement dismantled two smuggling gangs that flew cigarettes across the Belarus border by balloon and detained 27 people, including ten police officers and three border guards — the first known case of serving officers implicated in such a scheme. PM Ruginienė issued a public video address calling it an unprecedented case and demanded accountability from law-enforcement leadership; Interior officials said the detained officers would be suspended pending investigation.

stories.headline: FM Budrys says NATO could destroy Kaliningrad bases; PM Ruginienė and President Nausėda distance themselves
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys stated in an interview published around May 18 that NATO is capable of destroying all Russian military bases in Kaliningrad if necessary and accused Moscow of deliberately redirecting Ukrainian drones into Baltic airspace; Russia threatened nuclear retaliation and called his words 'madness.' PM Ruginienė publicly urged restraint from 'sharper statements,' characterising Budrys's remarks as 'deterrence rather than escalation rhetoric,' while President Nausėda said the interview was 'not the most successful' Lithuanian diplomatic communication.

stories.headline: Baltic presidents issue joint call for NATO air-policing mission to be upgraded to full air-defence mission
stories.summary: Following the week's series of drone incursions, the presidents of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania — including Gitanas Nausėda — issued a joint statement on May 21 calling on NATO to transition the Baltic Air Policing mission into a full air-defence mission with dedicated counter-drone capabilities.

stories.headline: Political pressure mounts on PM Ruginienė amid calls for LSDP leadership to take over government
stories.summary: The accumulated crises of the week — drone alert chaos, the registry data breach, and the officer-corruption scandal — intensified calls within and outside the coalition for PM Ruginienė to be replaced by LSDP party leader Mindaugas Sinkevičius; the acting leader of the 'Vardan Lietuvos' coalition partner stated she 'does not meet the qualifications' required of a prime minister, while LSDP loyalists defended her performance as adequate.

stories.headline: Nausėda condemns Russia's massive overnight drone and missile assault on Ukraine
stories.summary: President Nausėda publicly condemned Russia's large-scale overnight attack on Ukraine on May 24, which involved approximately 600 drones and 90 missiles including an Oreshnik ballistic missile, killing at least four people in Kyiv; Nausėda called it further evidence that 'terror remains Russia's primary war instrument.'

stories.headline: Bank of Lithuania takes enforcement actions against Paysera and Compensa Life for regulatory violations
stories.summary: The Bank of Lithuania issued two enforcement actions this week: it found that fintech firm Paysera LT had invested client funds in excessively risky securities and ordered corrective action by year-end; separately it fined the Lithuanian branch of Compensa Life Vienna Insurance Group €250,000 following a targeted inspection, with some clients to receive discounts as part of an administrative settlement.

stories.headline: Seimas passes Labour Code wage-transparency amendments to transpose EU directive
stories.summary: The Lithuanian parliament approved amendments to the Labour Code implementing the EU Pay Transparency Directive (2023/970), requiring employers to publish pay-gap data between men and women, disclose salary-setting criteria, and provide employees greater access to information about remuneration — with the changes needing to be in force by June.

stories.headline: Lithuanian housing market active but affordability declining as mortgage values rise 24%
stories.summary: Bank data shows Lithuanian banks issued Q1 2026 mortgage lending volumes roughly flat year-on-year but with average loan size up 24% and total value up 19%, driven by rising property prices in all major cities; Swedbank reported that housing affordability fell in all urban centres compared to Q1 2025, and projected the ECB would raise rates twice more this year.

stories.headline: Ignitis CEO argues green energy expansion requires strategic reserve capacity after Baltic grid synchronisation
stories.summary: The head of Ignitis Gamyba told Verslo žinios that following Lithuania's synchronisation with continental European power grids, reserve generation capacity has become both an economic and strategic security imperative, warning that renewable expansion without reserve backup risks grid instability; separately, an energy-sector commentator questioned whether Ignitis's planned small modular reactor projects would materialise on schedule.

stories.headline: Seimas advances LRT public broadcaster law amendments
stories.summary: The Seimas Culture Committee, led by Social Democrat Kęstutis Vilkauskas, advanced LRT law amendments prepared by a working group chaired by Speaker Juozas Olekas; the changes were described as reaching 'the finish line' of the legislative process this week.
